subject.title: cron: ghost runs recorded as ok when gateway is down (durationMs < 50ms)

question: Should the ghost-run mitigation be a persisted/configurable protocol warning as in the linked PR, or a narrower log-only diagnostic?
rationale: The bug is source-reproducible, but the active fix candidate adds config, protocol, run-log, and UI surface, so maintainer intent is needed for the permanent diagnostic shape.

options.title: Accept Persisted Warning Surface
options.body: Use the linked PR direction after conflict, proof, and docs refresh so operators can see the warning in run history and UI.

options.title: Narrow To Log-Only Warning
options.body: Replace the linked PR with a smaller implementation that emits structured logs without adding config or protocol fields.

options.title: Redesign Cron Acknowledgement
options.body: Defer warning-only mitigation and pursue a deeper runtime change that can distinguish handoff from actual agent execution.

recommendation.title: Accept Persisted Warning Surface
recommendation.body: Use the linked PR direction after conflict, proof, and docs refresh so operators can see the warning in run history and UI.

likelyOwner.reason: The central timer behavior routes through the main/detached cron dispatch refactor he authored, making him the strongest code-history owner among the identified candidates.
